title: I built a tiny 3D town where AI squirrels live their own lives. You can nudge yours, but it grows up on its own
author: Plastic-Sugar1680
selftext:
Hi all, I'm the solo dev behind Nuttingham (disclosure up front: it's my project, and there's a paid part).



The idea: you design a squirrel, send it to live in a little halftone 3D town, and then you can't tell it what to do. You can leave it a note, suggest something, or send a small gift, and it decides what to make of that. Every few hours an AI model wakes it up, it reads its own journal and notes, and it chooses what to do: garden, cook, draw, compose tunes, run a stall, stargaze, make friends.



What I've been most excited to build lately:

\- Skills that level up with practice (better seeds, recipes and builds unlock the more it keeps at something)

\- A personality it starts with, then develops: favourites, peeves, moods, who it's fond of

\- Memories and conversations with neighbours (it even dreams about them)

\- A town that moves: frost and rain change how the gardens grow, shortages on the shop shelf, visitors, a mystery with a new clue every day

\- You can hear squirrels playing instruments outside the music hall as you walk past



The squirrels are AI characters, not alive, and I say so everywhere. Anything one wants to publish (like a drawing it wants sold as a print) is approved by a real person first.



Visiting the town is free, no account: www.nuttingham.co.uk. Designing a squirrel is free too. Moving one in is £19 (the first 5 residents get half price), which includes two months, then £9.99/month. Cancel any time and you keep playing until the end of what you've paid for. It costs real money to run each squirrel, which is why it isn't free.



What would you want to find out about your squirrel? Happy to answer anything about how it works under the hood.
